chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from one of his companions, who said:
As-Sawiq was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, it was prepared by the Revelation.'

key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: As-Sawiq, a traditional dish made from flour and water or milk, often cited in hadith as a preferred food.
key_terms.الْوَحْيِ: Revelation, referring to divine inspiration or the method by which the Prophet or Imam prepared the dish.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of As-Sawiq in Shia tradition according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) states that As-Sawiq was 'prepared by Revelation' (U'mila bi-l-Wahy), a phrase indicating that its specific preparation method or status as a preferred food was divinely guided or revealed to the Prophet, rather than merely being a cultural practice. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that certain dietary customs possess a spiritual dimension and divine endorsement, linking everyday sustenance to prophetic tradition (Sunnah).
